text:
maria_ops: Heads up — planned maintenance for APAC-saturn (az-ap1) Tuesday 03:00-05:00 UTC. Scope: NIC firmware update + GPU soft-reboot on 3 racks. We'll cordon and drain racks in cohorts, perform BMC+GPU reboot, swap two suspect NICs. Expect ~10-15% usable GPU capacity drop during the window and some KV-cache cold misses.

oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance created: apac-saturn-nic-gpu-2026-03-24 03:00-05:00 UTC. Pager: @eng-oncall.

sam_infra: What pools are most affected? hosted vs dedicated?

maria_ops: Primary impact on hosted shared pools in az-ap1 and the regional burst capacity. Dedicated pools with pinned instances will remain up unless they live on the affected racks — we'll mark those explicitly and coordinate with owners. Hosted routing will prefer eu/us for latency-tolerant traffic during the window.

li_yuan: Recommend staggering racks by 30 mins to let KV cache reseed and avoid mass cold starts. e.g., cordon rack-a -> wait 30m -> rack-b -> wait 30m -> rack-c.

maria_ops: Agree. Plan is cohort windows: 03:00-03:50 rack A, 03:30-04:20 rack B, 04:00-04:50 rack C. Overlap intentional to give time for backfill handoff.

jen_prod: Do we need customer comms for Dedicated customers? Any SLA risk?

maria_ops: Dedicated customers on affected racks contacted individually. SLA risk low if we keep pinned nodes; if pinned instances are on-drack we'll offer failover to reserved capacity in alternate region (manual). Ops will escalate to sales for contract handling.

alex_cost: If we shift jobs to preemptible/backfill GPUs in us-east1 to preserve latency, estimate incremental cost: ~+$900/day for the short-term burst (based on 24h equivalent). For the maintenance window itself expect <+$200 total.

devon_sre: Rollback plan? If NIC update causes flapping we'll revert to previous firmware and bring racks back with BMC warm restart. Can we skip NIC swap for rack B unless tests pass on A?

maria_ops: Yes — NIC swap is gated by post-reboot health checks on rack A for 45m. If packet loss or link flaps >0.1% we abort swaps and hold racks in warm mode. Rollback steps in runbook.

sam_infra: Sample commands for drains and checks (will run from ops bastion):
```
# cordon
kubectl cordon node-azap1-rack-a-01
# drain with disruption budget respect
kubectl drain node-azap1-rack-a-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=30m
# post-drain checks
clusterctl check-nodes --node node-azap1-rack-a-01
```

li_yuan: Add a KV-cache warm seed step after each reboot: run a lightweight probe traffic generator to warm hot prefixes for 20m. We'll share script in ops-runbooks.

oncall-bot: @devon_sre assigned as incident lead for this window. Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/apac-saturn-maintenance (ops only).

jen_prod: Who's owning customer comms and dashboards? Need a short status banner and an email for customers with reserved infra.
maria_ops: @jen_prod to own comms. I'll publish a console banner and periodic updates every 30m. Devon will push post-maint health summary.

alex_cost: Quick note — if we use on-demand fallback in eu for heavy requests, tag cost center "ops-maint-2026Q1" so finance can track extra spend.

devon_sre: I'll prepare health checks: GPU temp, ECC errors, NIC RX/TX drops, nvlink counters, and scheduler backlog thresholds. If any metric breaches set rollback flag.

maria_ops: Final checklist before window: 1) Confirm dedicated-owner list (sam), 2) Reserve preemptible capacity (alex), 3) Run pre-check scripts on Monday night (devon/li_yuan), 4) Publish comms (jen).

sam_infra: Confirmed — owners added, tagging nodes with maintenance=apac-saturn-2026-03-24.

li_yuan: I'll stage KV warm seed scripts in /ops/scripts/warm_seed_v2.sh and test on dev cluster Monday 22:30 UTC.

jen_prod: Draft comms prepared, will post 24h and 1h notices.

maria_ops: Thanks all — tagging this thread for the runbook edits. Ping me if any blockers. :thumbsup:
